prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CCOc1cc2ncc(C#N)c(Nc3ccc(OCc4ccccn4)c(Cl)c3)c2cc1NC(=O)/C=C/CN(C)C
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL203

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of recombinant EGFR (unknown origin) after 10 mins by DELFIA/time-resolved fluorometry
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of epidermal growth factor receptor kinase (unknown origin) using [33P]-ATP after 20 to 30 mins by radiometric assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
INSUFFICIENT_INFO is not a valid response. You must commit to COMMENSURABLE or NOT_COMMENSURABLE.
If you lack direct evidence, make your best guess based on compound structure and target identity.
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.6, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 of EGFR kinase inhibition in biochemical (cell-free) formats with high confidence scores targeting the same human protein; while detection methods (DELFIA vs radiometric) and incubation times (10 min vs 20-30 min) differ slightly, for a potent irreversible covalent EGFR inhibitor (the compound contains a Michael acceptor acrylamide warhead), the IC50 values are expected to converge as covalent binding reaches completion, and differences in assay format typically yield results within 0.3 log units for well-characterized kinase targets."}
